summary: This project allows people who want to make space missions. The player can choose different difficulties depending on their skill and background and open their own space agency working for a chosen sponsor, the players can also compete in the leaderboard against real players and bots. The player is given a wide range of parameters and choices to make about their rocket design and takeoff, having to build a CML compliant design while taking into account their budget, as their agencies can go bankrupt after becoming insolvent. The game also gives feedback and tool tips on what the terminology in labels are as well as what failed and how to not fail again, helping the player understand and advance. Even if by itself it is *not* an encyclopedic source of knowledge, it can still help the player get accustomed to the terminology and procedures.
details:
Space Gaem: You Will Feel the Pain

Our Vision and Goal

- To give an opportunity to space cadets who wants to get experienced and learn space missions, rockets, the physics behind it etc. while being enjoyable.

- Making the game suitable for more people

Made using following the stack:

Node.js backend written in pure Typescript with Express.js for routing simple api calls and serving the page.

Three.js used for 3D rendering capability.

NASA GMAT (General Misssion Analysis Tool) for graphing Max-Q, suspecting failures by simulation, and giving the player feedback before launch.

The gameplay can be summarised as such:

- The player selects a difficulty and creates their agency (This is technically registration, but is required due to the multiplayer nature of the game)

- Is then given the choice of selecting a sponsor for their agency, each with their own caveats, then chooses a mission contract to proceed.

- After that, the player must go into the rocket builder to design the rocket, within the given budget, their agency will launch for the mission to deliver the given payload, they will choose the stages of the rocket as well as their size, type and fuel. Other parts such as a mandatory flight computer and disposable side tanks also exist.

- The rocket is subject to many CML (Concept maturity level) standards and must pass them as well as safety/risk checks before actual launch.

- After meeting all standards the player may launch the rocket and see a simulation, while I tried to make this accurate I'm not an actual scientist and therefore inaccuracies are expected, of the rocket proceeding towards the mission goal, with a live flight dashboard and event log.

- Finishing the mission the player can go to the debriefing page of the mission to see the overview of what happened, a rating of how they did, and what they gained, and may choose a new contract to continue playing.

What makes it seperate from the Other and the games benefits

-This game allows players to not just launch rockets, it provides a detailed design menu for the space cadets who wants to get better and have fun at the same

-This game could increase the number of space cadets

Our team considered:

1)Making the game realistic as we can

2)Budget mechanic

3)Being able to customize missions, rockets etc.

4)All the difficulties, Rocket design difficulties, Light/Dark Mode, Eye-saver modes to make it suitable for more people

5)Using NASA data & resources to save time and to be suitable for the rules
